_comment: Guided tour for drift correction in the emtk window. Targets are the spec's attr names and the windows and buttons the window draws; steps that need the user to act wait (await) and never press anything. The help page carries the long form.

steps.title: A drift of one pixel is a resolution of one pixel
steps.text: Anything that accumulates frames averages the drift into the result: a stage that wanders a pixel puts a pixel of blur into every structure. Each frame is cross-correlated with a reference and the correlation peak gives its displacement. This assumes pure translation: a rotating sample or a deforming cell is not corrected, and the giveaway is an erratic drift trace.

steps.title: Start with a stack whose answer you know
steps.text: Load example writes a bead stack that drifts by exactly (2, −1) px per frame and measures it, so you can check the tool against the truth before you trust it on your own data.

steps.title: Load the stack
steps.text: Your own data goes here: a frame stack or a photon stream (drop it on the ChiSurf window, then pick it in the Input section (the Datasets workspace)). It needs enough structure to correlate: a nearly empty field of view has no peak to find. Picking a file measures it at once.

steps.title: The reference decides which failure you get
steps.text: First frame: error never accumulates, right for slow monotonic drift. Previous frame: follows non-monotonic wander but small errors add up. Stack mean: the compromise for noisy data. None is universally right.

steps.title: Measure on one channel, correct them all
steps.text: The sample moves as a whole, so the shift is estimated from one channel and applied to every channel. Choose the brightest, most structured one: a flat channel gives a soft peak and an unreliable shift, which is then applied to the good channels too.

steps.title: Measure again after a change
steps.text: Changing the reference, the channel or the estimator does not re-run by itself. Measure repeats the measurement with the current settings.

await.hint: Press Measure and wait for the status line.

steps.title: Read the trace first, the images second
steps.text: Real stage drift is smooth and mostly monotonic. Erratic jumps mean the peak is found in noise, or the motion is not pure translation and this method does not apply.

steps.title: Wrapping or blanking
steps.text: Wrapping rolls what leaves one edge back in at the other: no signal is lost but the wrapped strip is meaningless. Blanking drops it and leaves the vacated strip empty. Crop before you measure anything near an edge. The Help button has the rest.
